tags.description: Concrete oil tanker (originally Old North State/McKittrick) converted into a gambling ship in 1932, run aground during a New Year's storm in 1937. The wreck lies in 1-6 metres of water off Coronado Beach, mostly buried under shifting sand. A historic curiosity rather than a premier dive site — only meaningfully exposed after major winter storms.
tags.name: SS Monte Carlo
tags.qa_notes: Depth corrected from 20m to 6m — wreck lies in 1-6m of water, not 20m. The OSM node depth was erroneous. Mostly buried under sand. tags.seamark:name: Sunken Harbor
tags.qa_notes: Sunken Harbor is the seafloor location name where HMCS Yukon was sunk. These coordinates are adjacent to the HMCS Yukon entry. The OSM node may refer to Wreck Alley complex generally. No separate named dive site 'Sunken Harbor' appears in published dive guides — it is the area designation, not an individual wreck. tags.description: WWII PC-461-class patrol submarine chaser, sunk September 11, 1945 in collision with USS Laffey in dense fog off San Diego Bay. One crew member lost. Navy demolition teams demolished the wreck in November 1945 and again in 1983, reducing it to a scattered debris field at 27 metres (90 fsw). Notable for early command by L. Ron Hubbard in 1943.
tags.name: USS PC-815
tags.qa_notes: Depth confirmed at 27m (90 fsw) per wreckedinmyrevo.com first-hand dive report. Site is a debris field, not an intact wreck — Navy demolition in 1945 and again in 1983 flattened most structure. Unexploded ordnance risk noted. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-04: added navsource.net (official NavSource Naval History archive) as a 3rd independent source, satisfying the 3-source validation bar. NavSource cross-check surfaced a tonnage conflict: Wikipedia states 295 tons displacement while NavSource states 450 tons — both figures are plausible for a PC-461-class subchaser depending on whether standard or full-load displacement is meant, but neither source disambiguates. Flagged as a sourced conflict in the markdown rather than picking one number. All other facts (builder Albina Engine & Machine Works Portland OR, commissioned 20 April 1943, collision with USS Laffey 11 September 1945, November 1945 Navy demolition) reconfirmed across both sources.

tags.description: Mackenzie-class Royal Canadian Navy destroyer escort (366ft/111m, pennant DDE 263) intentionally sunk July 14, 2000 at Sunken Harbor off Mission Beach as an artificial reef. The vessel sank prematurely in rough weather the night before the planned scuttling ceremony, rolling onto her port side. Water depth 30m (100ft); top of wreck at approximately 18m (60ft). At least five divers have died on this wreck — cold, dark, disorienting, with collapsed superstructure. Advanced certification required; wreck penetration requires specialist training.

tags.name: Wreck Alley
tags.qa_notes: Difficulty upgraded from Intermediate to Advanced — the deepest and most complex wrecks (HMCS Yukon at 30m, Ruby E at 26m) require advanced planning. Some wrecks (NOSC Tower at 18m) are accessible to intermediate divers. Wrecks: HMCS Yukon (DDE 263) 30m, Ruby E (ex-USCG Cyane, 1934) 26m, El Rey (kelp harvester) 23m, NOSC Tower 18m, Ingraham Street Bridge 18m. RE-AUDIT 2026-09-04: (1) El Rey depth corrected from 24m/80ft to 23m/75ft — ashunderwater.com and a cross-source aggregate both give 75ft; lajolla.com gives ~80ft, so a 75-80ft range is noted in the markdown. (2) El Rey years-of-service conflict found: Wikipedia and timesofsandiego.com say 35 years, lajolla.com says 41 years — flagged as a conflict rather than resolved. (3) Ruby E sinking date pinned to 18 July 1989 (specific time 3:30pm per ashunderwater.com) — previously only 'sunk 1989'. (4) Ruby E 'secret smuggling compartments delayed the sinking' detail, previously present in markdown, is now independently corroborated by ashunderwater.com (bulkhead compartments fore/aft of engine room) — added precise sourcing; one other source (wreckedinmyrevo.com, in a different article) calls the underlying smuggling story 'unverified family lore,' so the markdown notes that hedge. Added ashunderwater.com and wreckedinmyrevo.com to validation_source (now 6 domains).
